name.text: *** Using Geometric Formulas to Calculate Definite Integrals

questiontext.text:
Use the formula for the area of a circle to evaluate : \(\displaystyle \int_{@-radius@}^{@radius@} \sqrt{{@radius^2@}-\left({@var1-x^2@}\right)}dx\)

Note: You need to find the area under the curve over the interval \(\left [{@-radius@},{@radius@}\right]\).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

\(\displaystyle \int_{@-radius@}^{@radius@} \sqrt{{@radius^2@}-\left({@var1-x^2@}\right)}dx\)

Recall the equation of a circle is given as: \(\displaystyle x^2 + y^2 = r^2 \implies y= \sqrt {r^2-x^2} \)

We have the function

\(\displaystyle y= \sqrt{{@radius^2@}-\left({@var1-x^2@}\right)}\), and the interval {@-radius@}, {@radius@}

Let's first visualize the curve over the given interval as follows.

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [{#-radius-1#}, {#radius+1#}, {#radius+1#}, {#-radius-1#}], keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation: true }); // Creating points p and q. var point1 = board.create('point', [0, 0], { name: '' }); var point2 = board.create('point', [{#radius#}, 0], { name: 'q' }); var point3 = board.create('point', [{#-radius#}, 0], { name: 'p' }); // Creating the circle with center (0, 0) and radius {#radius#} var circle = board.create('circle', [point1, point2]); [[/jsxgraph]]

The limits of integration are from {@-radius@} to {@radius@}, which means we need to find the area of the semicircle between {@-radius@} and {@radius@}.

\(\displaystyle A =\frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 = {@decimalplaces(ta1,3)@}\)
